Allow me therefore to make something crystal clear:

I will NEVER be shamed into silence when it comes to one of the biggest issues of our time - *the political choice* to import thousands of men into this country, many of whom pose a risk predominantly to women & girls.

Nor will I ever be told by the likes of Matthew, which words I should use when describing a situation which catastrophically impacted mine & my families lives. When I said “standard domestic abuser”, his eyes lit up. He thought he had a ‘gotcha’. He did not. He thought he could hoist me with my own petard. He can not. 

There is a desperation by many people in the public domain to avoid accepting, or to underplay, the risk to women & girls that thousands of these imported men pose. Accepting the reality unravels their whole world view that “all people are equal” and that “diversity is our strength” and that there are “no alien cultures” etc…They fight for more “refugees to be welcome here”, comfortable that they are sheltered from the consequences. The lengths people are going to, to try & deflect attention from migrant crime is immense. As an example - We currently have a government spending our tax contributions trying to prevent data transparency in this area.

Oh & if you are someone who agrees with me, I promise you - “the problem in this country” is NOT us. Do not let Matthew or other people gaslight you. Just say NO. 

What is happening to this country is an absolute disgrace.

posts.text:
The biggest mistake that many people around the Zimbabwean president, Emmerson Mnangagwa, make is to confuse proximity to him with friendship. Mnangagwa was mentored by Robert Mugabe, and you see many of Mugabe's characteristics in how he behaves and deals with situations. 

He has no friends in politics. If someone tells you they are his friend, you are talking to a liar. His politics is built on your loyalty to him, not his loyalty to you, and many people fail to understand that. As far as he is concerned, he owes nobody anything, absolutely nothing. Everyone in his circle owe him everything because his decision to keep them is what makes them worthy in politics and business.

Look at how he has dealt with General Constantino Chiwenga. Look at Larry Mavhima, a relative who was at the centre of his escape. Look at Geoff Mbalekwa, his own nephew and the head of his security. Now look at where Mbalekwa is today. The only constant in Mnangagwa's life is his own interests, and nothing else.

Many people thought they were very close to Mugabe, and they discovered the folly of that belief. Mugabe crossed into Mozambique with Edgar Tekere, and the two suffered together. An ordinary mind would have forgiven whatever it thought Tekere had done, on the strength of that alone. 

They had known each other for almost 30 years in 1989, had been jailed together for ten years, had gone to Mozambique together and had come back to Zimbabwe together. Mugabe did not give two hoots about any of it. Mnangagwa learned from that.

There are people who go around town claiming to be Mnangagwa's nephews and nieces. I have spoken to a couple of people who know the president very well, and they tell me he finds it amusing and likes to keep those people believing they are very close to him. Everyone in that faction thinks they are the closest to the president. 

Whenever I have spoken to any of them in the past seven years, each one has told me that he is the closest. Many have fallen by the wayside. Some diplomats once believed that people said to be related to Mnangagwa were the right conduits or back channels, only to discover that it does not work like that with Mnangagwa. 

Rule number one for Mnangagwa is that if he made you, you must remain loyal. The minute you turn around, he will destroy you. He does not view General Chiwenga in that way, because he knows he did not make Chiwenga. Chiwenga is therefore not seen as disloyal. 

The people who are judged disloyal are those Mnangagwa made, who became his runners and then wanted to pretend they were their own men.
Go back and look at how he dealt with Mutumwa Mawere. They were like trousers and a belt, as we say in Shona. Yet Mnangagwa went after Mawere and destroyed him without saying a word, through actions alone. Mawere died broke and broken. That is Mnangagwa for you if you cross his redlines and were made by him.

Mnangagwa would rather tolerate a genuine opposition voice than a disloyal member of his own circle. If you are thrown into prison, you are lucky, because many people have suffered a worse fate. That has always been the rule in ZANUPF, and those who join that party without understanding it are making a grave mistake.

You could do a deal with Mugabe, and you can do a deal with Mnangagwa. But to assume that a deal makes you close to them, or that you now share friendship, is a fatal error, and many people must unlearn it. If you want to survive inside Mnangagwa's inner circle, remember that he knows everything everyone is doing. If you cross his line at the wrong moment, he will use that information to destroy you.

The stories about Angel were known for years, and people talked about them for years, just as they did about Magaya. His latest allegation was made a while ago. But he is paying for it now because he misunderstood his relationship to his boss. He was never Mnangagwa’s friend, he was a mere functionary.

To believe that being close to the president makes you immune from the vagaries of his system is idiotic. It is like believing that when a man invites you into his house, he is handing you the same powers he has in that house. You are just a visitor, the house belongs to the owner who invited you.

Pride and ego have brought untold suffering to those who assumed they were friends of Robert Mugabe or Emmerson Mnangagwa and expected these leaders to be loyal to them. They forgot that the duty of a follower is to be loyal to the leader, and in this case that leader is Mnangagwa.

Typical of Mnangagwa, we will know how upset he is with Angel by how this saga unfolds. Like Mugabe, he sometimes reminds you who the boss is by putting you through a public walk of shame, as Angel is going through now. He picks the worst of the crimes you are accused of, in this case sodomy, and tells the police to go ahead and do their work. The police know that when the president says so, they must go all out. The crimes are real, you were just being protected, but not anymore because you would have crossed the line.

Nobody of Angel's stature is arrested in Zimbabwe without the president approving it. Nobody is humiliated the way Angel was, picked up in an open pan truck. That is the ultimate humiliation for a man of his stature. The Ambassador at Large responsible for Europe and the Americas being picked up by armed police and driven in an open pan truck.
